title: There are sins people hide.
paragraphs: Then there are sins people baptize.
That second kind is more dangerous.

Because once lust learns how to quote Scripture, mimic intimacy with God, and speak the language of destiny, conviction starts sounding like persecution. Suddenly what should have led to repentance becomes “confirmation.” What should have been crucified becomes “God understands my heart.”
Because they trained themselves not to hear Him anymore.
“But here’s what most people don’t realize…”
The flesh does not always tempt you with rebellion that looks evil.
Sometimes it tempts you with spirituality that feels holy.
You can pray and still be in lust.
You can fast and still be in lust.
You can preach, lead worship, speak in tongues, post Bible verses, cry during worship… and still have a heart mastered by desire instead of God.
Jesus never said outward spirituality proved inward purity.
In fact, He warned the opposite.
“But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.”

It means:
“to covet,”
“to intensely desire,”
“to set one’s heart upon.”
A heart feeding itself forbidden intimacy.
Jesus places the battlefield in the heart before the body ever moves.
Because heaven sees sin earlier than humans do.

The modern world says:
“If you didn’t physically do anything, it’s fine.”

Jesus says:
“If your heart embraced it, heaven already witnessed it.”
When Lust Starts Wearing Church Clothes
One of the most deceptive forms of lust is not obvious immorality.
It is emotional-spiritual manipulation disguised as divine permission.
“The Lord told me this person is my kingdom partner.”
And because no one has “officially crossed the line,” people call it harmless.
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin…”
The Greek word for “drawn away” is:
It paints the image of bait dragging prey away from safety.
That is why hidden conversations matter.
That is why secret emotional attachment matters.
And the terrifying part is this:
People often ask God to bless what He already called impurity.
In Proverbs 7, Solomon describes seduction with terrifying precision.
The Hebrew language reveals something deeper than mere sexual temptation.
The strange woman says in Proverbs 7:14:
“I have peace offerings with me; this day have I paid my vows.”
The Hebrew phrase for “peace offerings” is:
These were legitimate sacrificial offerings connected to fellowship and communion.
She uses sacred symbolism to legitimize sinful desire.
Lust has always tried to wear spiritual garments.
And people still fall for it.
A worship leader can be in lust.
A pastor can be in lust.
A ministry team can be united by shared rebellion instead of shared holiness.
A relationship can sound spiritually mature while being completely governed by flesh.
Because spiritual language does not sanctify sinful motives.
“God Told Me” Is Not a Shield Against Sin
One of the most dangerous phrases in modern Christianity is:
Because many believers use God’s name to authorize what their flesh already decided.
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?”
Your heart can preach to you while betraying you.
That is why feelings are not final authority.
The Holy Spirit will never contradict the Word He inspired.
God will not bless adultery because you “feel peace.”
God will not authorize impurity because you “feel connected.”
God will not sanctify lust because worship music was playing while you felt it.
Feelings can be real and still be deceptive.
Samson Did Not Fall in One Night
Samson kept approaching what God warned him about.
Eventually desire blinded him before the Philistines ever did.
“Then went Samson to Gaza, and saw there an harlot…”
The Hebrew structure shows intentional movement.
That is why secret lust eventually reshapes theology.
People start changing doctrine to protect desire.
The Difference Between Conviction and Condemnation
Some people reading this feel exposed right now.
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus…”
But that same chapter also says believers must not walk after the flesh.
Grace is not permission to continue rebellion.
Grace is power to leave it.
The Greek word for grace is:
David did not collapse morally the moment he saw Bathsheba.
2 Samuel 11:1 says kings went to battle.
Idle compromise prepared the environment for lust.
Sin always costs more than it first promises.
And yet even David — broken, exposed, guilty — found mercy when he truly repented.
Psalm 51 becomes one of the most powerful repentance cries in Scripture.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God…”
That is the miracle of the Gospel.
Jesus does not merely restrain sin externally.
The Cross Did Not Come to Negotiate With Lust
Modern culture treats lust like personality.
“And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.”
The flesh does not retire peacefully.

And this is where many believers struggle:
they want intimacy with Jesus while protecting the very desires that nailed Him to the cross.
Or intimacy with God slowly suffocates.
Jesus and the Woman Caught in Adultery
In John 8, Jesus refuses both extremes.
He does not condemn her to destruction.
But neither does He excuse her sin.
“Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.”
But He does not celebrate sin to do it.
What Real Repentance Actually Looks Like
Real repentance is not emotional performance.
Not posting vague spiritual captions after secret compromise.
The Greek word for repentance is:
A change of mind resulting in changed direction.
Because people who truly hate sin stop protecting environments that feed it.
You knew that conversation was becoming dangerous.
You knew that attachment was becoming idolatrous.
You knew that “spiritual connection” was becoming emotional adultery.
But here is the hope most people miss:

The cross is powerful enough to cleanse sexual sin, emotional impurity, hidden fantasy, pornography addiction, manipulative relationships, secret conversations, spiritual hypocrisy, and years of compromise.
First Corinthians 6:9–11 lists sexual sins plainly.
“And such were some of you: but ye are washed…”
That is the power of Christ.
Because underneath all the excuses, deep down, you already knew the truth.
But Jesus is still calling you higher.
People who want truth even when it cuts first before it heals.
Kill what has been feeding it.
